transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you lately or what brings you in today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm having some issues with food. After my shifts—I'm a cashier—I just... I end up buying a lot of takeout. Like, really huge orders. Enough burgers and chicken and desserts for a whole family, I guess. And I just... I sit there and eat almost all of it myself before I even go home. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
When you're eating all that food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah... I guess. Um... it's just... once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me just... clicks off. Even if I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more'... I don't know. My hands just keep reaching for the next thing anyway. So... yeah.
When you're eating all that food, do you find yourself eating much faster than usual or eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Um... yeah. I don't really know about how fast I'm going, but... yeah. A lot of nights I just... I keep eating until my stomach gets really tight. It ends up hurting pretty bad. I usually just have to... lean the seat back in my car, or just go lie still in bed and wait for it to pass. So... yeah.
After you eat all that food, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or do anything else to try to compensate or get rid of the calories?
No... I don't do that. Um... I just wait for the stomach ache to go away, mostly. I've never tried to throw up or take anything like that.
After you eat all that food, do you feel really bad about yourself, like you're out of control or hate what you're doing?

Um... I'm not really sure. I don't... I try not to think about it too much after it happens. I mostly just... wait for the pain to stop so I can sleep. I don't really focus on... feeling anything about it, I guess.
Do you ever feel embarrassed or ashamed about how much you eat during these episodes, or try to hide your eating from others?

Um... yeah, I guess. I mean... I don't really do it around anyone. I'll just stay in my car in the parking lot, or... wait until my wife goes to bed. And I make sure to push the bags and receipts way down in the trash. I just... I don't want her to see all that.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're not in control of yourself, like you're just going through the motions without really thinking about it?

Um... yeah, I guess. It's just... once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me clicks off. Even while I'm sitting there telling myself, like, 'Demetrius, stop, you don't need any more'... my hands just keep reaching for the next thing anyway. So... yeah.
How often do these episodes happen? Like, how many times a week or month would you say this happens to you?

Um... a lot, I guess. For the last several months, it's been... maybe three or four nights most weeks. I don't know exactly. But... I can't remember a week where I didn't do it at least once. Not since the foreclosure calls started, anyway.
Do these episodes cause you a lot of distress, like feeling upset or worried about not being able to control your eating?
Um... yeah. I mean, it bothers me. I don't really want to be doing it. But... I don't know. It just happens.
Do you feel a sense of loss of control during these episodes, like you can’t stop eating even though you want to?

Um... yeah. Like I said a minute ago... once I take that first bite, it's like my brain just clicks off. I'll be telling myself to stop, but my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. So... yeah. I can't stop it. I don't really know how else to explain it.
Do these episodes of eating make you feel so upset or stressed that they affect your work, relationships, or daily life?

Um... I mean, I still show up for my cashier shifts. Work is fine. But... yeah, it causes some problems at home. I'm spending money on food that we really don't have right now. And... I don't tell my wife about it. So I'm just keeping secrets, and... it just makes things tense. It feels pretty dishonest.
